title: Worktops, fronts, plinths and gaps
intro: Coordinate worktops, fronts, plinths and joints through material, movement and maintenance requirements before fabrication.

sections.title: Document the top and cut-outs
sections.text: Document material, build-up, support, edges and joints. Sink/appliance cut-outs follow the approved template and worktop fabricator’s requirements, not a marketing size. Check sides, rails and underside fittings. A product change reopens cut-out and support review before cutting.
sections.caption: Coordinate product templates with worktop details.

sections.title: Coordinate fronts and gaps
sections.text: Draw front divisions, handles and the top/front junction. Give every gap a purpose, dimension and reference: motion, installation or appearance. Check that handles and top projections do not obstruct neighboring fronts or devices under the selected system.
sections.caption: Each defined gap needs a purpose and reference.

sections.title: Review plinths, access and junctions
sections.text: Show base, removable plinth and cleaning/service access. Do not conceal an airflow route required by the selected appliance. Record worktop/wall joints and joint materials with the relevant material supplier and identify inspection before concealing the detail.
sections.caption: The plinth is part of service coordination, not only appearance.

example.title: Worked case and decision
example.text: A replacement sink has the same marketed width, but its template and clips may differ. Hold cutting until the replacement template, rails, support and joint details are coordinated.
example.decision: Decision: approve the coordinated template before cutting.

quiz.question: Does the same marketed size justify reusing the sink cut-out?
quiz.explanation: Cut-out geometry and fixing details can differ by model.

assignment.prompt: Submit top/front/plinth sections, a cut-out/joint detail, references and hold points before cutting and concealment.

faq.question: Should every gap be identical?
faq.answer: No. Function and the selected system may require documented differences.
